transcription_uncertainties.detail: Selected world form is an editorial emendation (printed52 note4); final trembling form daggered (note5). Actual col312 explicitly cites20:2 for tremor. Tartarus remains only an editorial etymological suggestion, not adopted source replacement. Daggers enclose printed terminal punctuation as actually photographed.

translation.text: Urel, one of the holy angels—for he is concerned with the world and with “trembling.”[a]

footnotes.text: The list uses a short relation of the world and of trembling, introduced by for/because; concerned with supplies an English relation without adding a specific office or an unprinted appointment verb. The world expression is an editorial emendation in Charles printed52 note4. The noun trembling is enclosed by daggers; Dillmann1865 column312 gives that sense and explicitly cites20:2. Charles note5 suggests that the word may go back to a corrupt transliteration of Tartarus. This is his suggestion, not an independently verified name, and Tartarus is not silently substituted.

footnotes.text: The source gives a bare of-the-spirits relation, not an explicit over or appointed verb in this unit. Concerned with keeps that relation broad. Rufael follows the selected name, not a supplied variant from another angel list.

transcription_uncertainties.detail: Selected conjunction bracketed, called intrusion by note8; source dative relation not uncritically converted into world-of-luminaries or a fixed direction of vengeance.

translation.text: Raguel, one of the holy angels, who carries out vengeance concerning the world [and] the lights.[a]

footnotes.text: The conjunction and is bracketed in the selected edition; Charles printed52 note8 calls it an intrusion. The vengeance verb can express punishment or avenging on someone’s behalf. The source marks world and lights with ለ; concerning keeps that relation qualified instead of asserting a secure direction of vengeance. The world expression is not silently rewritten as the world of the luminaries.

translation.text: Mikael, one of the holy angels, for he was appointed over the best portion of humankind—over the people.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected verb is the passive appointed/commanded form ተአዘዘ, not the command-noun spelling suggested by raw OCR. Dillmann1865 column793 supports the appointed/commanded sense, and columns253–254 explicitly cite20:5 for the best-portion expression. The final source says the people; it does not name Israel here.

Actual note16 calls selected bracketed children-of-men phrase an intrusion. Corrects current OCR እስለ/እመሕያው segmentation and restores real star after final relative. No Greek replacement adopted.

translation.text: Saraqael, one of the holy angels, who is over the spirits [of the children of humankind] who sin in spirit.[a]

footnotes.text: This entire proposed unit remains held. The selected edition brackets “children of humankind” and calls it an intrusion (printed52 note16). The final starred plural spirit construction is uncertain: note17 asks whether it is accusative of limitation after the sin verb or a locative. “In spirit” is only a provisional way of displaying one possibility, not an approved resolution or an identification of the Holy Spirit; the singular English does not certify the plural source syntax. No Greek clause, later translation, or familiar angel roster is adopted to fill the uncertainty.
